title: Constructible sheaves
statement:
In this subsection $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$, so $\Dctf=\Dbc$ and we can argue with constructible
cohomology sheaves and standard truncations. A $\Lambda_X$-module is constructible
([sk-def-sfb-constructible]) exactly when it is *lisse*, that is locally free of finite rank
for the pro-étale topology, on each stratum of a finite stratification of $X$. For a locally
closed immersion $a\colon S\hookrightarrow X$, factor $a=i\circ u$ with
$u\colon S\hookrightarrow\overline S$ the open immersion into the closure and
$i\colon\overline S\hookrightarrow X$ the closed immersion, and put
$a_!=i_*u_!\colon\Mod(S_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)\to\Mod(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$. Both $u_!$
and $i_*$ are exact, so $a_!$ is exact, and it induces
$a_!\colon D(S_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)\to D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ without deriving.

Let $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$, and let $X$ be a standing scheme.

1. $\Cons(X,\Lambda)$ is closed under kernels, cokernels and extensions in
   $\Mod(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$. In particular it is an abelian category, and its
   inclusion into $\Mod(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ is exact.
2. $\Cons(X,\Lambda)$ is essentially small.
3. Every $F\in\Cons(X,\Lambda)$ has a finite filtration $0=F_0\subset F_1\subset\cdots\subset F_m=F$
   whose subquotients $F_k/F_{k-1}$ are of the form $a_!L$, with $a\colon S\hookrightarrow X$
   a locally closed immersion and $L$ a lisse $\Lambda_S$-module.

For a curve $X$, part (3) says that a constructible sheaf $F$ sits in an exact sequence
$0\to u_!L\to F\to i_*G\to0$, where $u$ is the inclusion of a dense open subset on which $F$
is lisse, $L=u^*F$, and $i_*G$ is supported on the finitely many closed points of the
complement.

external.place: *Kernels and cokernels.* On the topologically Noetherian scheme $S$, the kernel and cokernel of a morphism of lisse $\Lambda_S$-modules are lisse (Bhatt–Scholze, *The pro-étale topology for schemes*, Corollary 6.8.5); in particular its rank is locally constant on $S$, and no further stratification is needed.

*Kernels and cokernels.* On the topologically Noetherian scheme $S$, the kernel and cokernel of a morphism of lisse $\Lambda_S$-modules are lisse (Bhatt–Scholze, *The pro-étale topology for schemes*, Corollary 6.8.5); in particular its rank is locally constant on $S$, and no further stratification is needed.

The repleteness assertion of [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude] and a zero object in this abelian full subcategory give the ambient constructible property a zero object. Standard truncation retains each cohomology object or replaces it by zero; the existing proved homologyProperty_truncLE and homologyProperty_truncGE lemmas implement this, while the original lower and upper bounds give boundedness. In each of the two coefficient cases, apply [det-def-localizing-closure-ctf-equals-bc] with the identity monoid-object isomorphism to get Dctf=Dbc.

proof.text: Use the kernel, cokernel and extension closure classes supplied by [det-lem-coefficient-heart-closure]. Mathlib prop_kernel and prop_cokernel give the actual ambient objects. For an arbitrary exact pair, its zero-composite proof defines a ShortComplex; exact_iff_exact_toComposableArrows, the monomorphism and epimorphism produce its ShortExact proof. Apply prop_X₂_of_shortExact. Keep the abelianity and exact-inclusion witnesses from the same node.
Apply coefficientHeart_essentiallySmall from [det-lem-coefficient-heart-small] directly in the specified universe.

Choose an adapted lisse stratification by [det-lem-coefficient-heart-closure]. Lisse modules have finite constant models: inverse image from the point preserves finite biproducts of the regular module, so each finite free trivialization is the inverse image of the scalar finite free model (the proved private heart_free_model helper). Apply [det-lem-coefficient-heart-common-stratification] to the singleton family of this stratification to obtain an ordered adapted refinement R and its open prefixes. Apply [det-lem-coefficient-heart-filtration] to those prefixes. Use its counit image subobjects as T, its endpoints and nesting proof, and its quotient isomorphisms; reverse the order of the lisse and isomorphism witnesses to match the stated filtration predicate. This includes zero sheaves and empty schemes.

Choose an adapted lisse stratification by [det-lem-coefficient-heart-closure]. Obtain component generic points, their neighborhoods W and the actual surjective closed pullback projections from [lem-sfb-coefficient-heart-curve-generic-neighborhood]. Pull back each lisse stratum restriction to this fiber product. The canonical upperStarComp isomorphisms and the fiber-product equation identify it with the pullback of F restricted to W; descend by [lem-sfb-coefficient-heart-curve-lisse-descent]. Put U equal to the supremum of W. The inclusions W to U form a Zariski cover and hence a pro-etale cover. Compose its members with the finite-free trivializing covers to make F restricted to U lisse (the proved generic locFree_pullback, locFree_iso and locFree_of_cover helpers of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-locally-free-models], imported with import all). The neighborhood theorem gives density and containment of every component generic point, including the empty case.

Take the vanishing ideal of the closed complement of U and its actual reduced closed subscheme [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Apply [lem-sfb-coefficient-heart-curve-complement] with the generic-point containment just proved. Transfer its finite source along the closed immersion to finiteness of the complement, and express any complement point as the image of a source point for closedness. Retain its actual counit monomorphism, unit epimorphism, exact pair and vanishing open restriction of the closed term.
